threads.body: I think technically both name and version are required on the entity?

replies.body:
Both are recommended right now: https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/registry/entities/process.md#process-runtime

So the absence of both produces an empty id, which is not allowed, and then we skip producing an entity.

> Both are recommended right now: https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/registry/entities/process.md#process-runtime

Ah, I think that's a bug currently in the semantic conventions that is being fixed as schema v2 is rolled out.

see the [entity spec](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/entities/data-model/#identifying-attributes):

> If an observer cannot reliably obtain one or more identifying attributes, it MUST NOT emit telemetry using that entity type.

and [weaver schema v2](https://github.com/open-telemetry/weaver/blob/main/schemas/semconv-syntax.v2.md#entities-definition):

> `identity` - Required. List of [attribute references](#attribute-reference) that form the identity of the entity. These attributes uniquely identify an instance of the entity and are always required (`requirement_level` cannot be set on `identity` attributes).

threads.body: We don't have these constants yet from the java semconv repo, right? Next release?

replies.body:
Yup - just merged https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-java/pull/593

No release yet!

threads.body: [General] This guard requires both identifiers, but the PR promises an entity when either name or version is available. For example, a runtime name with no version produces only unassociated attributes. The linked entity definition marks both identifiers as Recommended, not Required. Fall back only when both are absent, emit the entity using the available identifier, and update the single-missing-identifier test cases to expect that entity.

replies.body: Updated PR description to match code, which is correct
